clue.text: Late finish prevents further progress

definitions.note: the clue describes what a blocked road or route does

parts.note: the late are the deceased, so late means dead
a finish is an end

explanation.surface: Turning up late ends one's chances of getting on.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind alley or hopeless course is one beyond which nobody can advance.

clue.text: How to upset grandee?

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it into disorder, so the letters of the noble's title are scrambled

explanation.surface: A question about how one might ruffle a Spanish nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals an anagram of GRANDEE, and the whole clue also describes the answer: to throw into disorder is a way to upset anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a person's mind or plans into disorder is a way of upsetting them.

clue.text: I'm in a race for life

indicators.note: the contraction is placed within the other pieces here

parts.note: a race or people can be called a nation
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be entered in a contest that decides life or death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a contest in the surface, but it means a people; 'life' in the sense of liveliness is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being full of vitality and liveliness is to have spirit, so the word is a synonym for life.

clue.text: Still without 'O' levels

definitions.note: a verb: flattens out or equalises

indicators.note: the letter in quotes is dropped from the phrase for nevertheless

parts.note: still, meaning nevertheless, is even so
the letter O as printed

explanation.surface: Someone who still has no O levels, the old British school exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the O from EVEN SO. O levels were British school exams at sixteen, which is the surface's trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To make things equal or flat is to level them; the verb in the answer means the same.

clue.text: The same herb is what should be taken

parts.note: ditto, abbreviated do, means the same
sage is a kitchen herb

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy, the same as before, is the one to take.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed amount of medicine is exactly what a patient ought to take.

clue.text: Used to season ticket, when with Minor County

parts.note: a tab is a ticket or label
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
county shortened, made minor, is Co

explanation.surface: A season ticket used with a minor county cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor Counties' are the English cricket counties below first-class level, which the surface leans on; here 'Minor' just means the county word is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery chilli sauce is a condiment added to flavour food.

clue.text: Strains to produce not easily obtained measures

parts.note: when money is tight it is hard to come by
ens are printers' measures of width

explanation.surface: Straining to produce measures that are hard to get hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain a rope or muscle is to make it taut.

clue.text: Looks flushed — needs plasma injection

definitions.note: describes eyes reddened, an adjective phrase

parts.note: plasma is the fluid part of blood
a shot is a jab or injection

explanation.surface: Someone looking flushed needs a transfusion of plasma.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes reddened with burst vessels give a flushed, red-eyed appearance.

clue.text: Black furry animal

definitions.meaning: in heraldry and poetry the colour black
a marten prized for its dark fur

explanation.surface: A dark-coated creature with thick fur.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic name for black is also a weasel-like mammal with valuable fur.

clue.text: Supervise or look after six deliveries

indicators.note: the word for look comes after the cricket term in the answer

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled
to look is to see

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on a cricket over of six balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over and direct work is to supervise it.

clue.text: They are very critical of the protection surrounding the Queen

indicators.note: the fence word goes round the royal abbreviation

parts.note: rails form a protective barrier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Barriers that protect the monarch from the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: People who rail against something complain bitterly about it.

clue.text: Leaving word with competent subordinate

parts.note: good means capable, as in good at a job
bye or by- means secondary, as in bye-law

explanation.surface: A capable underling has a word as they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The farewell said on departing is the word for leaving.

clue.text: Doesn't permit taking long view as this engenders confusion

indicators.note: a confusion jumbles things, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled thought on why someone refuses to take the long-term view.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia lets one see near objects clearly but blurs distant ones, so it stops one seeing far.

clue.text: Imagine I left the rest to unravel the mystery

indicators.note: to unravel is to untangle, so the remaining letters are rearranged
I has gone, so one letter I is taken from the first word

parts.note: the letter I as printed

explanation.surface: Picture someone walking off and leaving others to solve a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' drops one I from IMAGINE, giving IMAGNE; 'to unravel' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or riddle is something baffling and unexplained.

clue.text: A large number unfit and overweight, representing a serious handicap

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
unwell, ill
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Lots of unfit, overweight people are a real disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: A STONE is a British unit of body weight, fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy grinding wheel hung round one's neck is the image of a burden that holds one back.

clue.text: At the head of fashionable Commission

parts.note: in means in fashion
a charge is a duty one is commissioned with

explanation.surface: A trendy commission leading the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the person in command of something is to lead it.

clue.text: To send down a cutter is out of order.

indicators.note: out of order means not in sequence, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sending someone down for an improper cutter.
explanation.walkthrough: To send down is to suspend a student from a British university.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities suspend students by sending them away from college for a term.

clue.text: Stand-in performers get cramp before the crew

indicators.note: the growth word comes first in the answer

parts.note: to cramp growth is to stunt it
a crew is a body of men

explanation.surface: Doubles suffer cramp before the film crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubles who perform dangerous actions take an actor's place on set.

clue.text: Haircurling telephone rentals?

definitions.note: noun sense: curled locks of hair

parts.note: to telephone is to ring
lets are rentals of property

explanation.surface: Telephone rental costs that are hair-raising.
explanation.definitionFit: Long spiral curls of hair are the product of curling it.

clue.text: Describe how key company is taken in by little chap

indicators.note: the key and company go inside the word for the small fellow

parts.note: a runt is an undersized person
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: How a key firm is acquired by a small player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describe' is the definition in the sense of narrating a story; E is the key, and the container goes after the first letter of the little chap.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate or tell a story is to describe it.

clue.text: Holy man in present condition needs rest

parts.note: St is a saint
as is means in its current state

explanation.surface: A holy man, in his current state, needs a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of inactivity or stillness is a kind of rest.

clue.text: Pins down the sound of birds

indicators.note: says the seabird word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: skuas are predatory seabirds

explanation.surface: Bird calls that pin something down.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikes driven through to hold things are pins, and to drive them in fastens down.

clue.text: Where horses are fixed?

explanation.surface: Where the horses are kept secure.
explanation.definitionFit: A horses' building is a noun; firmly set and steady is the adjective sense.

clue.text: Going over with shipping company what happens in equatorial waters

parts.note: crossing is going over
a line is a shipping company, as in a cruise line

explanation.surface: Travelling with a shipping firm through tropical seas.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors passing the equator, 'the Line', traditionally hold a ceremony for first-timers.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing over the equator by ship is a sailors' rite of passage.

clue.text: One will have to believe in nothing before long

indicators.note: the zero comes ahead of the yearning word

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
to long is to pine

explanation.surface: Someone who must soon believe in nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold or state an opinion is to believe something.

clue.text: The best type

explanation.surface: The finest typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: The select few are the best; it is also a typewriter font of twelve characters per inch.

clue.text: A French one has a shape which is regular

parts.note: un is French for a
I is the Roman numeral one
form is shape

explanation.surface: A French figure with a consistent shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchanging and consistent throughout means even and regular.

clue.text: Army branch responsible for exploding a bridge

indicators.note: an explosion scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Army engineers given the job of blowing up a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit of several battalions is a formation within an army.

clue.text: The money round here is in the place indicated

indicators.note: the money word goes round the word for this place

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: The cash around here is in the stated place.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for cash; 'The' is only a link joining the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Within that spot or thing mentioned is the formal adverb's meaning.

clue.text: Small isolated places provide sound loopholes

indicators.note: tells us the little islands word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: islets are small islands

explanation.surface: Tiny remote spots give good escape routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Small holes for laces or cords, and the old slit in a wall, are loopholes.
